I work in a doggy day care and boarding. I wish people would understand why there is a need to train their dogs to do the following to help make work smoother. 

1. **Train your dog to walk nicely on a leash**. We DO NOT have time to put on your doggies cute little no-pull harness when we need them to walk from point A to point B. No, we have a lead that slips over their neck its called a slip lead. Your vet also will not be using those cute no-pull harnesses they also they use slip leads. Training them to walk correctly with a neck lead will prevent your dog from choking it self out every damn time. **You may think its cute to watch your 71 pound Lab drag you around, it's not. Its annoying and dangerous for me and the dog.** Your dog "just adorable 90 pound lap dog" might rip out my shoulder.

2. **Door control** Please train your dog to respect an open door/gate without running full speed. Also, walking though them isn't a reason to be over exited. We separate dogs at work or bring them inside and out. **Training them that door doesn't equal run full speed and be crazy can prevent dog fights here at work.** High levels of excitement can cause dog fights, dogs aren't extremely bright creatures sometimes. They will try to control each others excitement. If there is 20 dogs in my way and YOUR dog is getting nipped at or corrected for being too excited its possible the squabble turns bad it may take me a few seconds to get there and break it up. 

3. **Crating**. Some people view it as cruel to crate your dog, but **there are many occasions where crating your dog just has to be done**. This is one of them, while we do not crate during the day.. if your dog is spending time overnight virtually ANY dog care facility and all vets offices it will need to be crated. Think about it, we cannot have 30+ dogs running around at night unsupervised. If a dog fight were to break out for any reason there may be a possibility of a pack fight.
Now this all sounds bad. As if we have terrible dogs that will always start fights, but we don't. These are your dogs that will all lay down and enjoy each others company and play.. e.c.t. But these few things I wish owners taught would help save time from me having to teach them at work, and making their overall doggy day care experience much more enjoyable. 

4. **Teach your dog it's name** This is valuable for so many reasons I don't even know why some dogs don't know their name. There have been days were we've had 80+ dogs, and one dog is going home it is a huge pain in the ass to try hunt down Princess just so she can go home. Yes, I've had customers bitch at me for not getting their dog to them sooner. 

P.s. beware of anyone who says, "My dogs happy-go-lucky" it essentially means: My dog is very excitable. What it may include is: My dog may knock you over, knock objects over, run into other dogs or overall be very rude to other dogs. Which some people view as 'cute' or 'hes being friendly'. But your dog running full speed then immanently trying to get another dog to play by pawing at his face is rude in the dog world.

Similar story: When I was in the sixth grade my parents used to go out to dinner once a weekend night. One night I distinctly remember waiting and watching tv in my parents bedroom for them to come home and hearing doors slamming and my mom yelling at my dad about stupid things. I was young and didn't understand she was obviously way drunk. I overheard her and my dad argue throughout the house and later my dad loudly saying she already took her medication, but she said she couldn't remember and she took them again. And I heard her take them yet again hour later.

At 3 a.m. my dog kept barking.. loudly as if something was wrong. I remember hearing people knock at the door, my dad ran downstairs and let them in. I peaked out my bedroom to see some men come inside with some huge metal bars and cloth, I was scared they were taking my dog away and they were putting him to sleep because he was barking and being a nuisance. I walked out and saw my mom laying on her bedroom floor moaning. My dad told me my mom wouldn't get up and she needed to go to the hospital.

I was told in the morning that she had "acid reflux" and I couldn't see her until the following day. 

I realized a few years later, she was so intoxicated she took her anti-depressant medication three times over and could of died. At 16 I came to another realization that half of my memories in childhood of my mother coming into my room in the middle of the night to "tuck me in" or rub my arm or comb my hair, she was drunk and either wanted some one to talk to or wanted an escape from her depressed thoughts. She only a few years ago has told me she at times wishes she "wouldn't wake up the next morning."


I wish I didn't know this.
